topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Evolution and Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture themes and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer evolution and microenvironments.

topics.label: Genetic and Epigenetic Mechanisms of Clonal Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cell-intrinsic alterations provide selective advantages that drive clonal expansion and tumor initiation.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Hierarchical Stem Cell Models
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the role of normal tissue hierarchies and stemness properties in determining which cells can initiate and propagate tumors.

topics.label: Inflammatory and Microenvironmental Promoters of Tumor Initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how external promoters and inflammatory signals create the permissive microenvironment required for mutated cells to develop into tumors.

topics.label: Microenvironment Dependence in Established Tumors and Therapeutic Targeting
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains why established tumors require supportive stromal and inflammatory cells to grow and how targeting these microenvironmental components informs cancer therapies.

topics.label: Technologies for Mapping Tumor Evolution and Microenvironments
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic reviews genomic, transcriptomic, and spatial profiling methods used to investigate tumor clonal dynamics and cellular interactions.

topics.label: Comprehensive Synthesis of Cancer Evolution Factors
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes how genetic mutations, cell-of-origin stemness, and microenvironmental conditions jointly drive cancer evolution.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Next Steps
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on cancer therapies.
